record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: How are N = 1 vacua obtained from deformations of Seiberg-Witten curves explicitly linked to dessins d’enfants?

evidence.quote: Question 29. How are N = 1 vacua from Seiberg-Witten curves and dessins d’enfants explicitly linked?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $G$ be a simple gauge group and consider an $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetric gauge theory in four dimensions whose Coulomb branch is described by a Seiberg-Witten curve $\Sigma\to\mathbb{P}^1$ together with a meromorphic Seiberg-Witten differential $\lambda$. Adding a generic superpotential deformation that breaks supersymmetry from $\mathcal{N}=2$ to $\mathcal{N}=1$ confines the theory to isolated vacua, which are described by factorizations of the Seiberg-Witten curve in which the branch points coalesce so that $\Sigma$ degenerates to a rational curve with prescribed double points. To each such factorization one associates the corresponding rational map $\varphi:\mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$ obtained from the degenerated curve.

A Grothendieck dessin d'enfant is a bipartite graph embedded in a compact oriented surface that arises as $\varphi^{-1}([0,1])$ for a Belyi map $\varphi:X\to\mathbb{P}^1$, i.e. a rational map ramified only over $\{0,1,\infty\}$. Belyi's theorem implies that $X$ admits a model over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, and the absolute Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ acts faithfully on the set of dessins.

Problem. Construct an explicit and canonical correspondence
\[
\bigl\{\,\mathcal{N}=1\text{ vacua obtained from superpotential deformations of a given Seiberg-Witten curve}\,\bigr\}\;\longleftrightarrow\;\bigl\{\,\text{dessins d'enfants}\bigr\},
\]
specifying, for each $\mathcal{N}=1$ vacuum, which Belyi pair $(X,\varphi)$ it produces and, conversely, which factorization data of the Seiberg-Witten curve correspond to a given dessin. The correspondence should identify gauge-theoretic invariants distinguishing branches of $\mathcal{N}=1$ vacua with arithmetic invariants distinguishing Galois orbits of dessins, and should be compatible with the natural moduli of the Coulomb branch.
artifact.status_search_result: An explicit link has been developed in several works, beginning with "Children's Drawings From Seiberg-Witten Curves" (2006) and substantially extended in "Dessins d'enfants, Seiberg-Witten curves and conformal blocks" (JHEP 2021), where Belyi maps are identified with degenerated Seiberg-Witten curves and combined with AGT to produce conformal blocks; a machine-learning exploration also exists. The correspondence is constructed in specific families (e.g. trivalent dessins with 4 punctures on the sphere) and connects gauge-theoretic branch invariants to Galois-orbit invariants, but a fully general, canonical dictionary remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Children's Drawings From Seiberg-Witten Curves
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies Seiberg-Witten curves with polynomial equations used to construct dessins d'enfants; gauge theory criteria distinguishing branches of N=1 vacua yield invariants distinguishing dessins in different Galois orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Initial explicit link between N=1 vacua from SW curves and dessins.

status_evidence.title: Dessins d'enfants, Seiberg-Witten curves and conformal blocks
status_evidence.snippet: Maps Grothendieck's dessins to algebraic curves as Seiberg-Witten curves, then via mirror map and AGT to N=2 instanton partition functions and Virasoro conformal blocks; explicit treatment of 6 trivalent dessins with 4 punctures on the sphere.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a refined and partial explicit correspondence.

status_evidence.title: Machine-Learning Dessins d'Enfants: Explorations via Modular and Seiberg-Witten Curves
status_evidence.snippet: Explores via ML the relations between dessins, modular curves, and Seiberg-Witten curves.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that the correspondence is not exhaustively understood and remains under active investigation.
